result.reasoning:
Every factual sub-claim in the finding checks out, but the inference that makes it a defect does not, and does not reproduce.

Verified true: `n_gen = max(1, ceil(budget/population_size))` (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/mining/gp.py:735), so budget fixes generations only and 192/48 gives 5x48 = 240 slots; `GPMiner._score` memoises on `expr.key()` (gp.py:430-435) so a repeated tree is free and never increments `ParturaScorer.n`; `child = self.generator.crossover(a, b) or a` (gp.py:684) and the non-crossover branch `child = self._select(...)` (gp.py:686) both hand back an already-scored population member; /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json really does show steer scored=123 / control scored=170 at budget 192, population 48, seed 0; and /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:336 really is `A["efficiency_per_100"] = 100.0 * len(heads) / max(A["scored"], 1)`.

Refuted: the claim that "这 38% 恰好等于 170/123,完全来自重复槽位被缓存吞掉的比例,与干预质量无关". `heads` and `scored` live on the SAME set — distinct paid evaluations. `scored` counts distinct keys reaching the scorer; `live = scored - gate_fail` exactly in evidence.json (123-21=102, 170-40=130), the archive holds one entry per distinct non-gated key (`_archive_update`, gp.py:549-562), and `passers`/`heads` are subsets of that archive. A duplicate slot adds to neither the numerator nor the denominator, so the duplicate ratio cancels: `heads/scored` is an unbiased estimate of the per-paid-evaluation hit rate, which is exactly what the module docstring says is being compared ("of the candidates each arm paid to evaluate, how many pass the gates").

My reproduction ran AlphaCube's real breeding code with idea_search.py's real hooks and confirmed the described mechanism fires hard in the steer arm (251.8 `acceptable` rejections per run, crossover->None 12.8/131.5, 79.7 free cache hits vs control's 62.8, scored 160.3 vs 177.2 — a 10.6% gap from precisely this mechanism), while holding the true per-distinct-tree hit rate identical in both arms by construction. Result: `efficiency_per_100` ratio steer/control = 0.97-0.99 at every head rate tested, not the 1.106 the finding predicts; `heads` instead track `scored` (ratio control/steer 1.12-1.14, matching the 1.106 scored ratio). The metric is not inflated by duplicates.

The failure scenario's "若两臂各找到 1 个 head" is an assumption, not a consequence: it conditions the numerators equal while the denominators differ. With equal intervention quality that is a 12-13% coincidence in my sweep (P(exactly 1 head in both arms) = 0.130 at p=0.006, 0.122 at p=0.010, 0.033 at p=0.020), not the systematic outcome. If both arms genuinely find 1 head off 123 and 170 paid evaluations, steer genuinely had the higher hit rate per evaluation — that is the measurement, not an artifact of it.

Two further reasons not to act on this. (a) The reported numbers were never printed: both arms have `passers = 0` in evidence.json, so `allp` is empty, the `if allp:` block at idea_search.py:300-339 never ran, and no `efficiency_per_100` key exists in either arm. The "steer 0.81/100 vs control 0.59/100" line is hypothetical. (b) The reporter's own probe does not reproduce the 38% either — it reports steer 165 vs control 192 (16%), and I get 10.6%; the real run's 123-vs-170 gap is therefore mostly not this mechanism (steer's wall time 1341s against control's 3105s on near-equal scoring_seconds, 503 vs 618, points at the steer arm's run ending early, which `except Exception` at idea_search.py:270-272 would swallow silently). Either way the rate metric stays unbiased.

Separately, the suggested fix is not implementable as written: `ProgressFn = Callable[[int, int, dict], None]` (gp.py:50) and `mine` discards the callback's return value (gp.py:755-759, 776-782), so no `on_generation` callback can stop the loop, and the script's stated contract is that nothing in AlphaCube is edited.

The only residual (non-numeric, out of scope per the brief) observation is reporting hygiene: `passers` is a volume and `efficiency_per_100` a rate, so they can move in opposite directions. The script already prints `scored` on the same line as `passers` (idea_search.py:291-292), so the denominator is not hidden. Recording `slots = population*(n_gen+1)` in evidence.json would be nice to have, but no reported number is wrong.

Scripts written (nothing outside tmp/review, no existing file touched, no commit, no server):
/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/budget_denominator/repro.py (first attempt, confounded by cross-run key overlap — documented in its own header)
/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/budget_denominator/repro2.py (decisive unbiasedness test)
/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/budget_denominator/repro3.py (mechanism-is-live check plus the finding's own rare-head scenario)
result.reproduction:
Setup (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/budget_denominator/repro2.py and repro3.py): bind AlphaCube's real GPMiner._next_generation / _select / _mutate onto a bare object with the production parameters idea_search.py passes (population 48, min_depth 2, max_depth 4, crossover_rate 0.7, mutation_rate 0.3, elitism 1, tournament 3, merge 0.8, cull 0.5), install idea_search.py's real `pick`/`acceptable` hooks for I2_dispersion_fold from guidance/B01.yaml, and run 1 initial population + 4 generations = 240 slots, exactly as mine() does for budget 192. Replace the reward with a synthetic one memoised on expr.key() just as GPMiner._score is, where gate failure and head-ness are independent uniform hashes of the key -- so the intervention has ZERO effect on the per-distinct-tree hit rate by construction. 40 GP seeds; head draw averaged over 500-2000 independent salts to decorrelate runs.

Mechanism is live (repro3.py, part 1):
  steer    slots 240  free cache hits 79.7  paid 160.3   acceptable rejections 251.8   crossover->None 12.8/131.5
  control  slots 240  free cache hits 62.8  paid 177.2   acceptable rejections   0.0   crossover->None  0.8/132.8
  scored control/steer = 1.106   <- the exact lever the finding names, firing

Metric is NOT inflated (repro2.py):
  steer    heads mean 10.152   eff/100 mean 6.337
  control  heads mean 11.442   eff/100 mean 6.455
  true per-paid-evaluation head rate = 100*0.08*(1-0.20) = 6.400 -- both arms recover it
  heads control/steer = 1.127  (tracks scored, does NOT stay equal)
  eff   steer/control = 0.982  (finding predicts 1.106)

The finding's rare-head scenario (repro3.py, part 2), equal true hit rate in both arms:
  p=0.006: heads 0.757 vs 0.864 (c/s 1.141); eff 0.473 vs 0.487 (s/c 0.970); P(exactly 1 head in BOTH arms) = 0.130
  p=0.010: heads 1.270 vs 1.430 (c/s 1.126); eff 0.793 vs 0.807 (s/c 0.983); P = 0.122
  p=0.020: heads 2.550 vs 2.856 (c/s 1.120); eff 1.591 vs 1.611 (s/c 0.988); P = 0.033

Conclusion: the duplicate-slot gap in `scored` is real and reproduces, but it propagates into `heads` at the same rate, so `efficiency_per_100` stays at the true per-evaluation hit rate (ratio ~1.00) instead of being inflated by scored_control/scored_steer. No wrong output was produced; the failure scenario's premise (equal heads, unequal denominators) is assumed rather than caused. Also confirmed the real run never printed the metric at all: evidence.json has passers=0 for both arms, so idea_search.py:300-339 did not execute and no efficiency_per_100 key exists.
